synopsis: The corpus identifies substantial research datasets, including SODA with 19,846 construction images, MOCS with 41,668 images reported in a September 2026 preprint, and LiDARDustX with 30,000 mining-truck lidar frames, more than 80% dusty [f10825, f10826, f7065, f7066]. Their availability does not establish collision-warning validity: the discussed construction datasets are image-only with fixed or aerial viewpoints, and no off-road collision-warning validation was found for RELLIS-3D, RUGD, GOOSE or TartanDrive [f5845, f5851]. Simulation benchmarks also require real-data checks: simulated versus real RELLIS-3D data showed large domain shifts, while S2R-Bench highlights failures to predict real weather robustness [f4741, f776]. Major gaps include job-site ultrasonic and thermal material data and large off-road naturalistic interaction datasets; these limit sensor modeling and the defensibility of rare-event evaluation claims [f3717, f6859, f7277]. The adverse-weather gap is stated more categorically in the glossary than in Chapter 6, which acknowledges MINE4DRAD and real-dust lidar exceptions; planning should therefore assess the manufacturer's existing fleet recordings and their machine, site and weather coverage before deciding what additional data can be collected [f12822, f5102, f12823, f272].
